The Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps has disbanded its Anti-Vandalism Outpost in Gombe State following a shooting incident involving its personnel and a truck driver at New Mile 3. The State Commandant, Muhammed Usman, also summoned all officers-in-charge of the various formations and outposts in the state for an emergency meeting on Friday to address the incident and reinforce discipline among personnel. The development followed a misunderstanding between operatives of the Anti-Vandalism Unit and a truck driver on Thursday, November 12, which resulted in the discharge of a firearm. In a statement issued on Friday, the command’s Public Relations Officer, Buhari Sa’ad, said the meeting was convened to address the incident and reinforce professional standards among personnel. During the meeting, Usman cautioned officers against unprofessional conduct, indiscipline and actions capable of tarnishing the image of the corps. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources He stressed that personnel must remain professional, disciplined and civil while respecting the fundamental human rights of members of the public in the discharge of their duties. 2027: Tinubu orders crackdown on thuggery, violence Police probe attack on Pantami’s convoy in Gombe NOA takes anti-vote buying, violence campaign to Gombe communities The commandant said, “The use of firearms must be guided strictly by established rules, operational procedures and applicable regulations,” warning that no officer should take the law into his or her hands under any circumstances. As part of the disciplinary and administrative measures, Usman ordered the immediate disbandment of the Anti-Vandalism Outpost and directed all personnel attached to the unit to report to the state command headquarters without delay. He said, “The Corps will not condone any act of indiscipline, abuse of authority or violation of the rights of citizens.” The commandant also urged outpost commanders to strengthen supervision of their personnel and ensure strict compliance with professional standards, discipline and accountability. He assured residents that the command remained committed to protecting lives and property, respecting human rights and maintaining peace and order in Gombe State. Chima Azubuike
